newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico overnight Cetes rate rises to 19.40 pct.
newsitem.headline: Mexico overnight Cetes rate rises to 19.40 pct.

text.p: Mexican overnight Cetes rates closed 40 basis points higher at 19.40 percent, traders said on Friday.
"Rates had come down so much that those who had money hung on to it. They weren't prepared to buy so low," a trader said.
Traders said rates had declined for most of the session, amid a strengthening of peso. The Mexican currency rose against the dollar as U.S. bond yields slipped.
Benchmark 48-hour peso contracts closed 2.5 centavos firmer at 7.7690/7.7710 per dollar.
Yields on U.S. 30-year Treasury bonds receded to 6.53 percent from 6.63 percent on Thursday.
Overnight rates on bank paper ended 40 basis points lower at 20.60 percent.
Banco de Mexico offset surplus liquidity in the market by draining 1.985 billion pesos through four auctions.

Despite concerns among some traders about the eight-week decline in primary rates, others said the continuing strength of the peso and ample secondary market liquidity could pave the way for further primary rate cuts at next week's auction.
Rates on bellwether 28-day Cetes were assigned at 19.69 percent last week.
Traders said the central bank's decision to offer more long-term paper at next week's auction, and less short-term issues, was a sign that rates were expected to continue to fall.
In its weekly call for bids, Banco de Mexico announced five-year UDI bonds for the first time and cut back on the amount of 28-day, 91-day and 182-day Cetes on offer.
"It will be important to see how much demand there is for these rates, as a sign of how much confidence there is," one dealer said.
Liquidity of 6.250 billion pesos was scheduled to return to the market on Monday. Dealers said liquidity could tighten as Pemex withdraws cash to meet a tax payment.
